pr_title: input/tablet: add seatop_down entry for tablet input
pr_body:
Depends on https://github.com/swaywm/wlroots/pull/2158.

Currently, when tablet input exits a window during an implicit grab, it
passes focus to another window.

For instance, this is problematic when trying to drag a scrollbar, and
exiting the window — the scrollbar motion stops. Additionally,
without `focus_follows_mouse no`, the tablet passes focus to whatever
surface it goes over regardless of if there is an active implicit grab.

If the tablet is over a surface that does not bind tablet handlers, sway
will fall back to pointer emulation, and all of this works fine. It
probably should have consistent behavior between emulated and
not-emulated input, though.

This commit adds a condition for entering `seatop_down` when a tablet's
tool tip goes down, and exiting when it goes up. Since events won't be
routed through `seatop_default`, this prevents windows losing focus during
implicit grabs.

Closes #5302.

Some more logic should be refactored into these new handlers, but I feel
that is best left outside the scope of this PR.

issue_context.title: Tablet implicit grab stops sending motion events when outside surface
issue_context.body:
For example, this is problematic when trying to drag a scrollbar, and exiting the window — the scrollbar motion stops. Additionally, without `focus_follows_mouse no`, the tablet passes focus to whatever surface it goes over regardless of if there is an active implicit.

If the tablet is over a surface that does not bind tablet handlers, sway will fall back to pointer emulation, and all of this works fine. It probably should have consistent behavior between emulated and not-emulated input, though.

review_comments: Shouldn't this be inside the condition above, right after `seatop_tablet_tool_motion`?
Can't we send events in the `tablet_tool_tip` handlers instead?

Hmm, I'm not sure I follow... do you mean within the seatop handlers for `tablet_tool_tip`? We do send the actual motion events in the seatop handler for `tablet_tool_motion`, but deciding whether to emulate input as pointer events is a task that seems best left to `cursor.c`, so that all the special-casing can happen in one place as opposed to over different seatop implementations.

That leaves the seatops receiving only pointer and tablet input, without having to worry about whether it's _emulated_ pointer input they're receiving, or "real" input.

I agree that emulating pointer events is something that should be done in `cursor.c`. However calling functions that directly send events like `wlr_tablet_v2_tablet_tool_notify_proximity_out` is a little fragile here. The seatop may or may not forward events to `wlr_seat`, in case it doesn't, we shouldn't notify proximity out.

But I see we don't have `sway_seatop_impl.tablet_tool_proximity_out` yet, so my point is moot anyway. Also looking at this PR now, the diff doesn't touch the code near `wlr_tablet_v2_tablet_tool_notify_proximity_out` (though maybe that has changed with the rebase? can't remember).

tl;dr LGTM!
